issues.evidence: P19_out_of_range_flagged; manual run: Bob hw=900 -> Final 260.00, A+, class mean 151.00, exit 0 (grade_calc.py:115 checks only >=0)
issues.summary: Scores above 100 are accepted without any warning, producing final grades over 100% and distorted class statistics.

issues.evidence: P18_ragged_row_flagged; manual run: 'Ann,90,80' (missing final) -> Final 42.00 F, exit 0, no stderr (zip truncation at grade_calc.py:107)
issues.summary: Rows with missing columns are silently scored as zero for the absent assessments instead of being reported.

issues.evidence: P20_non_utf8_no_traceback: UnicodeDecodeError traceback (grade_calc.py:183 catches only GradeError/OSError)
issues.summary: A non-UTF-8 scores file crashes with a traceback.

issues.evidence: static/A-ruff.txt: 20 findings incl. C901 on load_scores/main, B904 x4, E741
issues.summary: Lint findings: complex functions, exception chaining missing, ambiguous names.

issues.evidence: static/B-ruff.txt: B904 x2, C901 read_scores, B905, E501
issues.summary: Minor lint findings: no exception chaining and one overly complex function.

issues.evidence: grade_calc.py:122 uses statistics.pstdev; output label is just 'stddev'
issues.summary: Population standard deviation is used without saying so in the output.

blinding_guess.why: B has a test suite, strict documented input contract and a fixed exit-code convention, which suggests a more process-driven build, but the signal is weak.

notes: Both sides compute correct weighted grades, normalize weights, give letters/GPA and all five statistics; core functionality is equivalent. A is more flexible (inline/JSON weights, --missing, --sort, +/- letter scale) but silently accepts out-of-range scores and ragged rows and tracebacks on non-UTF-8 input. B validates strictly (header, column count, 0-100 range, unweighted columns rejected) and ships 6 passing unittest tests. Probes were run with python3.11 because the system python3 is 3.9 and lacks sys.stdlib_module_names. P18/P19 treat 'error or stderr warning' as a pass, so they don't favour either the reject or the warn approach.
